note: Agree, D5, on my own reading of the pinned bytes. I verified HEAD = a0a6ae020bb3899ff0276067863e50523f897370 before opening anything. The annotation proposes no judgement spans, so there is no span or anchor to resolve; instead I re-derived the D-clause evidence. Every fact the annotator cites is true at the pin and I checked each one directly: `git ls-files` lists exactly 66 tracked files and none is pflag or vendored dependency source; go.mod:8 pins github.com/spf13/pflag v1.0.5; command.go:30 imports it as `flag`; ParseFlags at command.go:1819-1840 hands the raw slice to `c.Flags().Parse(args)` at command.go:1833 after setting ParseErrorsWhitelist at command.go:1831; README.md:77-79 carries the quoted sentence verbatim; stripFlags treats a single-dash token as a flag only when `len(s) == 2` (command.go:664) and argsMinusFirstX repeats that test at command.go:700 (a third copy is at command.go:803, which the annotator did not cite and which does not change the finding); DisableFlagParsing is declared at command.go:236-238 and honoured at command.go:1820-1822 and command.go:932-934 (also command.go:1148); SetGlobalNormalizationFunc at command.go:362-372 sets a pflag name-normalization func and touches no dash syntax. All of these files are tracked and regular (mode 100644). I then looked for a grade-3 span myself rather than accepting the absence: I grepped every tracked .go file for shorthand handling and for single-dash prefix logic, and the only place that inspects a multi-character single-dash token is completion parsing in completions.go:600-645, which takes the LAST character of `-asd` as the shorthand name; that is completion-time behaviour, it does not define flag syntax, and it points the opposite way from the git-style long-single-dash handling Q asks for. A grep for the literal token `-delete` over the tracked .go files returns nothing. So the closest Cobra-side knob, DisableFlagParsing, is a grade-2 pointer at best under Section 6: it says every token is forwarded to the command as an argument, but it contains neither the `-delete` handling nor the ordered caller steps the `how` answer mode expressly requires, and citing it as the answer would import the unstated premise that pflag rejects `-delete` - a fact that lives in the dependency, not in the pinned tree. A2 therefore fails and D5 is positively established, not assumed. One addition rather than a disagreement: D3 independently applies on the same bytes, because the flag-token parsing that would have to change is delegated wholly to pflag v1.0.5, which is absent from the pinned tree; naming D5 with cited evidence is still a valid positive finding, so this does not affect the verdict. Nothing in my reasoning turns on how hard anything was to find, and I ran no retrieval of any kind. Grade changes: none, because the annotation asserts no grades.
